pr.title: Merge dead bb pruning and unreachable bb deduplication.
pr.description:
Both routines share the same basic structure: iterate on all bbs to identify work, and then renumber bbs. 

We can do both at once.

processing.reason:
The PR (rust-lang/rust#119699) is a pure structural refactor of MIR CFG cleanup: it merges `remove_duplicate_unreachable_blocks` into `remove_dead_blocks` and makes `Inline` delegate to `simplify_cfg`. The frozen analysis itself classifies it as "a structural/optimization defect rather than a demonstrated semantic miscompile." Both the old two-pass scheme and the new single retain/renumber pass compute the same observable program behavior:

- Dead-block pruning only removes blocks that `reachable_as_bitset` marks unreachable; deleting unreachable blocks cannot affect any concrete execution.
- Empty-unreachable-block deduplication only merges blocks whose entire body is `unreachable;`. Such a block can never complete normally, so redirecting successor edges from one `Unreachable` terminator to another is observationally equivalent. The old pass also deduplicated not-yet-dead blocks; that is extra work, not a value change.
- The change in which empty unreachable block is retained and the resulting block renumbering are purely cosmetic; they only alter MIR printed block indices, as the updated `.diff`/CHECK-line test expectations confirm.

The supplied test diffs show only block-index renumbering and removal/relocation of `unreachable;` blocks (e.g. `otherwise: bb30` → `otherwise: bb9`, `bb7: unreachable` removed), never changed assignments, control-flow decisions, or return values. There is no historical value-level wrong transformation to encode: producing two Rust functions that differ on concrete inputs would require inventing a semantic change unrelated to this PR, which the instructions forbid. Therefore no source-grounded original/transformed pair with differing defined behavior can be validated.

analysis.originalLogic: `SimplifyCfg`'s `simplify_cfg` performed three sequential steps: `CfgSimplifier::new(body).simplify()`, `remove_duplicate_unreachable_blocks(tcx, body)`, then `remove_dead_blocks(body)`. `remove_duplicate_unreachable_blocks` independently scanned all basic blocks for empty unreachable non-cleanup blocks (using `bb.terminator.is_some() && bb.is_empty_unreachable() && !bb.is_cleanup`), collected them into an `FxIndexSet<BasicBlock>` regardless of reachability, and if more than one existed rewrote every terminator successor equal to a duplicate to `duplicates[0]`. `remove_dead_blocks` then separately computed `traversal::reachable_as_bitset(body)` and retained/renumbered only reachable blocks. `Inline` duplicated part of this logic manually via `CfgSimplifier::new(body).simplify(); remove_dead_blocks(body);`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical transformation being replaced is the split two-pass prune/deduplicate scheme: deduplicate empty unreachable blocks in a standalone pass over the entire body (including blocks that are themselves unreachable and about to be deleted), then in a second pass compute reachability and renumber. This has the same basic structure twice ("iterate on all bbs to identify work, and then renumber bbs") and does deduplication work on dead blocks that will not survive. It is a structural/optimization defect rather than a demonstrated semantic miscompile. The replacement must perform reachability-based dead-block pruning and empty-unreachable-block deduplication in one retain/renumber pass, and must only deduplicate blocks that are actually reachable.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR `Body` CFGs before/after `CfgSimplifier::simplify`, especially bodies containing one or more empty `TerminatorKind::Unreachable` non-cleanup basic blocks and/or blocks unreachable from `START_BLOCK`. Relevant producers include `SimplifyCfg` itself, `Inline` (which now delegates to `simplify_cfg`), `ConstGoto`, `DeduplicateBlocks`, `EarlyOtherwiseBranch`, `MatchBranchSimplification`, `RemoveUnneededDrops`, and `SeparateConstSwitch`.
analysis.summary: Historical merged refactor of `SimplifyCfg` that folds unreachable empty-block deduplication into dead-block pruning/renumbering inside `remove_dead_blocks`, restricts deduplication to reachable blocks, and makes `Inline` call `simplify_cfg` instead of manually invoking `CfgSimplifier` plus `remove_dead_blocks`.
analysis.trigger: `remove_dead_blocks` is entered when the body has unreachable blocks or more than one reachable empty unreachable block: the early return is guarded by `if num_blocks == reachable.count() && empty_unreachable_blocks <= 1 {`. Deduplication is triggered by reachable blocks satisfying `bbdata.terminator.is_some() && bbdata.is_empty_unreachable() && !bbdata.is_cleanup`, counted via `.filter(|(bb, bbdata)| should_deduplicate_unreachable(bbdata) && reachable.contains(*bb))`.
preconditions: The body is a MIR CFG on which CfgSimplifier::simplify has run; this can leave unreachable blocks without a terminator, so code must tolerate bbdata.terminator.is_none().
Multiple empty unreachable blocks may exist; only those in the reachable bitset may be deduplicated: reachable.contains(*bb).
Cleanup blocks must not be merged with non-cleanup blocks: the predicate requires !bbdata.is_cleanup.

The first surviving reachable empty unreachable block is retained via let kept_unreachable = *kept_unreachable.get_or_insert(used_bb); later duplicates are dropped and their original indices map to the kept renumbered block.
Inline previously did its own CfgSimplifier + remove_dead_blocks sequence and must use the unified simplify_cfg so it gets deduplication as well.
pitfalls: Do not collect empty unreachable blocks without checking reachability; the old standalone dedup pass did so, whereas the merged routine filters with reachable.contains(*bb).
Do not deduplicate cleanup blocks against non-cleanup blocks, even if both are empty unreachable.
Do not assume every basic block has a terminator when deduplicating: CfgSimplifier::simplify can leave terminator-less unreachable blocks, and the predicate checks bbdata.terminator.is_some().
Do not preserve the old early-return condition based only on num_blocks == reachable.count(); it must also allow work when empty_unreachable_blocks > 1.

The replacements map must redirect a dropped duplicate to the retained renumbered block (replacements[orig_index] = kept_unreachable) before renumbering successors; otherwise terminator targets can refer to removed blocks.
Keep deduplication and pruning in the same retain pass; doing them separately requires two scans/renumberings and can deduplicate blocks that are about to be removed.
A retained empty unreachable block may now appear at a different (usually later) block index than in the old output; MIR test expectations must be updated for block renumbering.
analysis.testStrategy: Use the mir-opt harness to dump MIR after a pass that invokes `simplify_cfg` and assert CFG shape with CHECK lines: construct a body with at least two reachable empty `unreachable;` blocks and verify only one remains, that all successor edges targeting the duplicates point to that single retained block, and that all unreachable blocks are gone with blocks renumbered. Add a case with a cleanup empty unreachable block and a non-cleanup one to confirm they are not merged, and a case where CfgSimplifier leaves a terminator-less block to confirm pruning remains safe. Test through both `SimplifyCfg` and `Inline` so the delegated `simplify_cfg` path is covered. Run panic-abort and panic-unwind variants because unwind edges change which blocks are reachable. Inspect regenerated mir-opt `.diff` files for expected block-number shifts; no compiler was built here, so these are construction/validation strategies rather than executed results.
evidence: Merge dead bb pruning and unreachable bb deduplication.
We can do both at once.
